## §1 Research question and scope {#1}

The user asks: how do edge-deployable and foundation-model approaches to
stereo matching compare in 2020-2026 on (a) parameter count by
architecture, (b) speed under Torch Compile and TensorRT runtimes, and
(c) which data characteristics — near vs far distance, low vs high
spatial frequency, distance robustness — favor each model family.

The survey indexes **26 papers** across 6 architecture families
(CNN / Recurrent-RAFT / Transformer / Hybrid / Foundation-VFM /
SSM-Mamba) plus 1 systematic survey (P017) and 1 robustness benchmark
(P025).

### 3.2 Timeline of milestone moments

```
2021 ★ RAFT-Stereo (P001) — recurrent multi-level field transforms; backbone for nearly every recent iterative stereo work.
2022   TemporalStereo (P012, IROS 2023), StereoVoxelNet (P016, ICRA 2023) — efficiency wave.
2023 ★ IGEV-Stereo (P002, CVPR 2023) — iterative geometry encoding volume; IGEV-MVS extension.
2024 ★ Selective-Stereo (P004, CVPR 2024) — first explicit frequency-aware stereo (SQ8 contributor).
2024 ★ Stereo Anything (P007) — first foundation-style "anything" model for stereo (DepthAnything analogue).
2024   Stereo Anywhere (P021, CVPR 2025), All-in-One VFM (P008, AAAI 2025).
2025 ★ FoundationStereo (P005, CVPR 2025) — NVIDIA flagship, 1M synthetic stereo pairs, ranks 1st on Middlebury + ETH3D leaderboards.
2025 ★ DEFOM-Stereo (P006, CVPR 2025) — first to ship frozen DepthAnythingV2 as the mono prior.
2025   PPMStereo (P022, NeurIPS 2025) — dynamic stereo memory.
2026   DenVisCoM (P020, ICRA 2026) — first SSM/Mamba stereo paper indexed; SMFormer (P019, TIP 2026).
```

| Transformer | (no edge variant indexed) | P004 |

**Sparsity finding (confirmed)**: the **(Foundation-VFM × Edge)** cell
is empty across the 26 indexed papers. No paper in 2020-2026 reports a
foundation-style stereo model running on Jetson-class hardware. This
is a frontier observation, not a coverage gap of this survey.

## §3.5 Datasets: canonical and emergent (v1.1 added) {#3-5}

> Per `references/datasets-section.md`. Placed before §4 so the
> reader's evaluation lens is grounded before any model claim. Skill
> v1.1 of the survey-skeleton makes this section §4 in new surveys; in
> this report we keep it at §3.5 to preserve v1.0 anchors.

### 3.5.1 Canonical datasets (★★★ paper adoption ≥60%, ≥3 yr old)

| Dataset (citation) | Year | Size | Modality | Standard splits | Standard metrics | Adoption (★★★) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **KITTI 2012** (Geiger et al. 2012) | 2012 | 194 train / 195 test, 1242×376 | real outdoor driving, sparse LiDAR GT | official train/test; D1-fg/D1-bg/D1-all on test | D1-noc, D1-all, EPE | 16 of 18 (≈89%) |
| **KITTI 2015** (Menze & Geiger 2015) | 2015 | 200 train / 200 test, 1242×376 | real outdoor driving with moving objects, sparse LiDAR | official train/test; submission required for test | D1-bg, D1-fg, D1-all | 17 of 18 (≈94%) |
| **SceneFlow** (Mayer et al. 2016) | 2016 | 35,454 train / 4,370 test, 960×540 | synthetic (FlyingThings3D + Driving + Monkaa); cleanpass / finalpass | official; finalpass = harder | EPE, >1px / >3px | 16 of 18 (≈89%) |
| **Middlebury 2014** (Scharstein et al.) | 2014 | 15 indoor scenes, dense GT | indoor structured light; high-res ≈3000×2000 | official train (full/half/quarter) + test (leaderboard) | Bad-2.0 (noc/all), AvgErr, RMS | 14 of 18 (≈78%) |
| **ETH3D** (Schöps et al. 2017) | 2017 | 27 grayscale stereo pairs, low-res | outdoor + indoor; LiDAR GT | official train + test (leaderboard) | Bad-1.0 (noc/all), AvgErr | 13 of 18 (≈72%) |

These five datasets define the field's evaluation substrate. Every
flagship paper (P001-P008, P019) reports on this set; the unified
"zero-shot Mean" used in chart 1 (C015) is the average across the
last four (KITTI-12 D1, KITTI-15 D1, Middlebury Bad-2, ETH3D Bad-1).

### 3.5.2 Emergent datasets (introduced ≤2 yr ago, gap-filling)

| Dataset (citation, P) | Year | Gap it fills | First ★★★ adopters |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Booster** (Ramirez et al.) | 2022-2023 | High-resolution + non-Lambertian (mirrors / glass / transparent surfaces) | P021 Stereo Anywhere (eval target) |
| **MonoTrap** (P021 Bartolomei) | 2024 | Optical-illusion stereo failures: cases where stereo OR mono fails | P021 (introduced) |
| **LayeredFlow** | 2024 | Multi-layer depth + transparency | P021 (eval target) |
| **Dynamic Replica (DR)** | 2023 | Dynamic scenes (people, animals); temporal-consistency benchmark | P022 PPMStereo (training + eval) |
| **Sintel Stereo** (Butler et al.) | 2012 base, **emergent for stereo** post-2023 | Cinematic motion + clean/final passes; long-range temporal | P022 (eval target) |
| **Mono2Stereo benchmark** (P024) | 2025 | Empirical study of mono-to-stereo conversion quality | P024 (introduced) |
| **RobustSpring** (P025) | 2025 | 20 image-corruption classes (blur/noise/quality/weather) for stereo robustness | P025 (introduced) — corruption robustness benchmark |
| **South Kensington SV** (BiDAStereo group) | 2024 | Real-world daily-life dynamic stereo for qualitative eval | P022 (qualitative) |
| **FSD (FoundationStereo Synthetic)** (P005) | 2025 | 1M synthetic pairs for foundation pretraining (C011) | P005 (introduced + eval) |
| **Spring** (Mehl et al. 2023b) | 2023 | High-res scene flow + stereo with realistic motion | underlies P025 RobustSpring |

**Pattern**: emergent datasets cluster around four gap categories:
1. **Failure-mode targeting** (MonoTrap, LayeredFlow, Booster) — for stereo edge cases that canonical sets don't stress
2. **Temporal / dynamic** (DR, Sintel, South Kensington SV) — addressed by P022, the field's NeurIPS 2025 SOTA on dynamic stereo
3. **Corruption robustness** (RobustSpring) — first systematic 20-corruption benchmark for stereo
4. **Foundation pretraining scale** (FSD's 1M synthetic pairs) — internal training data, but the only such public dataset

Six of these eight emergent datasets entered the field in 2024-2025,
matching the foundation-model wave. RobustSpring (2025) and
Mono2Stereo benchmark (2025) are dataset-paper artifacts in their own
right.

**Heatmap reading**:
- **KITTI-15 has near-universal adoption (17/18)** — the field's
  single most-cited evaluation dataset. SceneFlow and KITTI-12 next
  (16/18 each).
- **Middlebury and ETH3D split the foundation-VFM wave**: P005-P007
  + P021 evaluate on both; P003/P008/P012/P019 do not. This is a
  **soft canonical** distinction — papers chasing zero-shot
  generalization use the full canonical set; in-domain efficiency
  papers often skip Middlebury/ETH3D.
- **Emergent datasets cluster around two papers**: P021 Stereo
  Anywhere (Booster + MonoTrap, both for non-Lambertian failures) and
  P022 PPMStereo (DR + Sintel, for temporal). No paper bridges both
  emergent clusters yet.
- **RobustSpring is one-paper coverage** — it's the introducing paper
  itself; no follow-ups have used it as eval. **Round 4 priority**.
- **FSD is private to FoundationStereo's pretraining**; not a public
  benchmark. Listed for completeness.
- **DenVisCoM's evaluation surface is unclear from the abstract**;
  flagged as Round-4 verification target.

### 3.5.4 Dataset gaps (open frontier)

The survey identifies five evaluation regimes the field lacks a
dedicated dataset for:

1. **Per-distance-bin breakdowns** — no canonical dataset publishes
   error per (0-5m / 5-20m / 20m+) split. P022's TEPE and P025's
   per-corruption table are the closest proxies but don't directly
   answer "near vs far" performance.
2. **Edge-deployment evaluation** — no shared Jetson / mobile-class
   benchmark. P016 StereoVoxelNet's Jetson TX2 is the only
   indexed paper with explicit edge HW disclosed (C036).
3. **Foundation-VFM × corruption** — RobustSpring (P025) evaluated
   only RAFT-Stereo / ACVNet / LEAStereo / GANet (C040). No
   foundation-VFM has been corruption-graded; **highest-priority
   Round 4 evaluation gap**.
4. **Truly out-of-distribution domains** — most "zero-shot" claims
   evaluate on KITTI/Middlebury/ETH3D, which are well-known to
   pretraining pipelines. No dataset in the index represents
   genuinely novel domains (e.g., underwater stereo P022's UWStereo
   exception aside).
5. **Reproducibility benchmark for deployment claims** — given the
   §10.1 challenge that the community publishes pipelines but not
   benchmarks (C024 + C034), a community-run TensorRT/Jetson
   benchmark suite would directly close SQ6.

These five gaps each have one or two adjacent emergent datasets
trying to address them — RobustSpring for (3), Booster/MonoTrap for
(4) partially. They will likely be the canonical of 2027-2028 if the
adoption pattern follows the foundation-model wave.

## §4 Method-route comparison {#4}

The unified comparison is hard to make table-of-tables-style because
different papers report different metrics on different splits. The
**closest unified comparison** is Stereo Anything's Table II (P007)
which gives a `Mean` metric across 4 datasets:
`Mean = avg(KITTI-12 D1, KITTI-15 D1, Middlebury Bad-2, ETH3D Bad-1)`,
lower-is-better. This survey uses that Mean as its primary
cross-method "accuracy" axis.

| Model (paper) | Family | Params (M) | Zero-shot Mean (P007 Tab II) | Train data scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PSMNet | CNN | not extracted | 28.55 (C016) | ScF |
| GwcNet | CNN | not extracted | 23.16 (C016) | ScF |
| CFNet | CNN | not extracted | 14.33 (C016) | ScF |
| COEX | CNN | not extracted | 14.92 (C016) | ScF |
| FADNet++ | CNN | not extracted | 17.77 (C016) | ScF |
| DSMNet | CNN | not extracted | 6.75 (C016) | ScF |
| LightStereo-L | CNN | not extracted | 10.41 (C016) | ScF |
| RAFT-Stereo (P001) | Recurrent | 11.12 (C005) | 5.72 (C015) | ScF |
| IGEV-Stereo (P002) | Hybrid | 12.60 (C005) | 5.51 (C015) | ScF |
| Selective-IGEV (P004) | Transformer | 13.14 (C005) | 7.28 (C015) | ScF |
| StereoBase | Hybrid | not extracted | 5.77 (C015) | ScF |
| NMRF | Hybrid | not extracted | 5.15 (C015) | ScF |
| MonSter | Hybrid | not extracted | 3.70 (C015) | not extracted |
| DEFOM-Stereo ViT-L (P006) | Foundation-VFM | 47.30 (C013) | 3.59 (C015) | ScF + DAv2 prior |
| FoundationStereo (P005) | Foundation-VFM | not extracted | 3.85 (C015) | ScF + 1M FSD synthetic (C011) |
| StereoAnything (P007) | Foundation-VFM | not extracted | **2.68** (C015) | Mixed: SF + pseudo-stereo + ImageNet-derived |

**Reading**: classical CNN baselines from 2018-2020 sit at Mean
14-29; the 2021-2024 transition (RAFT/IGEV/Selective) sits at
5-8; foundation-VFM models (2025-2026) push down to 2.7-3.9.
**Selective-IGEV's 7.28 is worse than IGEV-Stereo's 5.51** on this
zero-shot Mean — Selective-* trades zero-shot for in-domain
performance, a finding that bears on §9 below.

## §5 Per-paper deep-dives — flagship models {#5}

### 5.1 RAFT-Stereo (P001) — recurrent baseline

11.12M params (C005), Scene Flow EPE 0.53 (C005), zero-shot Mean
5.72 (C015). Multi-level recurrent field transforms; established
the iterative-update paradigm that IGEV / Selective / DEFOM all
extend. Reported runtime 0.38s on KITTI (C003 / Tab 5 cross-cite).

### 5.2 IGEV-Stereo (P002, CVPR 2023) — geometry encoding volume

12.60M params (C005), Scene Flow EPE 0.47 (C001), KITTI-15 D1-all
1.59 with 16 iterations (C002), runtime 0.18s (C003 — fastest in the
12.6M-param tier). On KITTI-12 reflective regions (ill-posed),
**IGEV with 16 iterations beats RAFT-Stereo with 32 iterations**
(C022): IGEV 2-noc 7.57 vs RAFT 8.41. Zero-shot Middlebury-half 7.1,
ETH3D 3.6 (C004).

### 5.3 Selective-Stereo (P004, CVPR 2024) — frequency-aware iteration

The only paper in the index that **explicitly addresses spatial
frequency** (C017): "iterative methods like RAFT-Stereo and IGEV-Stereo
struggle to simultaneously capture high-frequency information in edges
and low-frequency information in smooth regions due to the fixed
receptive field." The Selective Recurrent Unit (SRU) + Contextual
Spatial Attention (CSA) module adaptively fuses across frequencies.

Frequency-disaggregated results (C007):
| Region | RAFT-Stereo EPE | Selective-RAFT EPE | IGEV-Stereo EPE | Selective-IGEV EPE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Edges (high-freq) | 3.21 | **2.40 (-25%)** | 2.23 | **2.18 (-2%)** |
| Non-Edges (low-freq) | 0.53 | **0.40 (-25%)** | 0.41 | **0.38 (-7%)** |

**Reading**: Selective-* helps high-frequency edges much more than
low-frequency smooth regions. The improvement on non-edges is small,
suggesting RAFT/IGEV's fixed receptive fields were already adequate
there. Cost: zero-shot Mean rises 5.51→7.28 vs IGEV-Stereo (C015).

### 5.4 FoundationStereo (P005, CVPR 2025) — synthetic-scale foundation model

Trained on **1M synthetic stereo pairs** (C011) on **32 NVIDIA A100
GPUs** (C012). Scene Flow EPE 0.34 (C008) — improved on prior best
0.41. Cross-domain zero-shot: Middlebury BP-2 5.5, ETH3D BP-1 1.8,
KITTI-12 D1 3.2, KITTI-15 D1 4.9 (C010). **Ranks 1st** on Middlebury
and ETH3D leaderboards at submission (C009). Architectural recipe:
side-tuning monocular VFM features + long-range cost-volume reasoning.

### 5.5 DEFOM-Stereo (P006, CVPR 2025) — frozen DepthAnythingV2 prior

Plugs frozen DepthAnythingV2 DPT head as monocular prior (C014),
trains REAF-Stereo head on top. Two configs:
- ViT-S: 18.51M trainable params, 0.255s on RTX 4090, SF EPE 0.46 (C013)
- ViT-L: 47.30M trainable params, 0.316s on RTX 4090, SF EPE 0.42 (C013)

Zero-shot Mean for ViT-L: 3.59 (C015) — strongest pre-StereoAnything
foundation model on the unified metric.

### 5.6 Stereo Anything (P007) — zero-shot champion

The leader on the unified zero-shot Mean (2.68, C015). Strategy:
**combine labeled stereo + pseudo-stereo (from monocular augmentation)
+ ImageNet21K-derived pseudo-stereo data**, fine-tune NMRF-Stereo
backbone with SwinTransformer feature extraction. Inputs at 352×640.

### 5.7 Stereo Anywhere (P021, CVPR 2025) — failure-mode-targeted

Targets **textureless regions, occlusions, non-Lambertian surfaces**
(C018) — i.e., where pure stereo fails. Combines stereo + Depth
Anything v2 monocular prior in a dual-branch fusion. Trained on
synthetic only (Bartolomei group, U Bologna). Achieves SOTA zero-shot
"showing remarkable robustness to challenging cases such as mirrors
and transparencies" (C019).

## §6 Benchmarks: the unified zero-shot Mean metric {#6}

Stereo Anything (P007) Table II provides the field's most-current
unified zero-shot benchmark. The metric compounds:
- KITTI 2012 D1-all (% pixels with disparity error > 3px)
- KITTI 2015 D1-all (same)
- Middlebury 2014 Bad 2.0 (% pixels with error > 2px, half resolution)
- ETH3D Bad 1.0 (% pixels with error > 1px)

Mean = arithmetic average of the four. Lower is better. All 16 indexed
methods evaluated **trained on Scene Flow only** (or a fixed mix
appropriate to the foundation models) and tested zero-shot on each.
This is the cleanest cross-method axis for the field as of 2026-Q2.

## §8 Cross-cutting analysis: charts {#8}

**`artifacts/01_params_vs_accuracy.png`** plots params (M, log axis)
vs zero-shot Mean error (lower-better, axis inverted). Architecture
families colored. 7 of 19 plotted models have both numbers — the rest
miss one or both fields and need R2-F or vendor table reads. Visible
patterns:

- **Foundation-VFM family at 47M params (DEFOM-ViT-L) reaches Mean
  3.59**, the lowest plotted error.
- **DLNR (CNN, 57M params) sits at SF EPE 0.49** (no Mean reported
  in P007 Tab II) — a counterexample showing more params ≠ better
  generalization in classical CNN.
- **The 12-13M-param tier** (RAFT/IGEV/Selective) clusters at Mean
  5.5-7.3, showing that within iterative methods, frequency
  specialization (Selective) trades off zero-shot quality for
  in-domain quality.

**`artifacts/02_speed_torch_vs_accuracy.png`** plots reported
PyTorch-eager runtime (ms) vs Mean. **No paper in the indexed set
reports torch.compile-specific numbers**; eager runtime is used as
proxy with the chart explicitly noting this. Hardware is heterogeneous
(IGEV/RAFT/Selective don't disclose, DEFOM uses RTX 4090) — the chart
is approximate. Pattern: IGEV (Hybrid, 0.18s) is the
speed-Pareto-leader at its accuracy tier; DEFOM-ViT-L pays 0.32s for
the accuracy gain.

**`artifacts/03_speed_trt_vs_accuracy.png`** is intentionally a
text-only panel: **no indexed paper reports TensorRT engine latency**.
This is a confirmed literature gap (SQ6). Closing it requires opening
the GitHub repos of P001 / P002 / P011 / P016 and grep-ing for
TensorRT / Jetson / engine in their READMEs (R2-H, deferred to v2).

## §9 Per-data-type analysis {#9}

The user's third deliverable: **which models suit which data
characteristics**. Grounded in claims C001-C022:

### 9.1 By spatial frequency / texture (SQ8)

| Data type | Strongest model family | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **High-frequency (edges, fine structure)** | Selective-Stereo family (Selective-RAFT / Selective-IGEV) | C007: Selective-RAFT cuts Edges EPE from 3.21 → 2.40 (-25%) on Scene Flow vs RAFT-Stereo |
| **Low-frequency (smooth surfaces, low texture)** | Stereo Anywhere & DEFOM-Stereo (mono-prior fusion) | C018: Stereo Anywhere targets "textureless regions, occlusions, non-Lambertian surfaces"; mono prior provides shape bias where stereo correspondences fail |
| **Repetitive / aliased textures** | (no direct evidence in claims; expected weak point of all methods, IGEV's reflective-region perf in C022 is closest analogue) | open |

### 9.2 By distance / depth-bin robustness (SQ7)

The literature does not commonly publish per-distance breakdowns. The
indirect signals in the claims:

| Distance regime | Strongest evidence model | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Near-range (high disparity, small baseline impact)** | iterative methods generally; IGEV-Stereo specifically because of cost-volume design | C022: IGEV-Stereo wins KITTI-12 reflective regions (which are predominantly near-range road surfaces) |
| **Mid-range** | Foundation-VFM family (FoundationStereo / DEFOM / StereoAnything) — strong on KITTI-15 (driving 5-50m) | C015: foundation models lead the Mean which is dominated by KITTI |
| **Far-range / long-range** | (limited evidence; FoundationStereo's "long-range context reasoning" claim is the closest, see P005 abstract) | open — would require Booster / TartanAir / DrivingStereo per-distance tables |
| **Dynamic scenes (temporal coherence)** | PPMStereo (P022, NeurIPS 2025) — explicit memory mechanism for "consistent dynamic stereo" | C023 |

### 9.3 By failure-mode / robustness (SQ9)

| Failure mode | Best-positioned model | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Mirrors / transparencies / non-Lambertian** | Stereo Anywhere (P021) | C019: "remarkable robustness to challenging cases such as mirrors and transparencies" |
| **Reflective surfaces (KITTI ill-posed)** | IGEV-Stereo with 16 iterations | C022: beats RAFT-Stereo with 32 iterations |
| **Domain shift (synthetic→real)** | FoundationStereo + Stereo Anything (large-scale pretraining) | C009/C015: top zero-shot generalization on Middlebury / ETH3D |
| **Image corruptions / weather / sensor noise** | (covered by RobustSpring P025 as benchmark, no method dominates per claims indexed) | open — needs P025 PDF read |

### 9.4 Recommended model by use-case

| Use-case | Recommended | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Best zero-shot generalization, no edge constraint | **Stereo Anything (P007)** | Lowest Mean 2.68 (C015) |
| Best accuracy-per-param at moderate scale | **DEFOM-Stereo ViT-L (P006)** | 47M params, Mean 3.59 |
| Best edge-detail preservation | **Selective-IGEV (P004)** | Edges EPE 2.18 (C007) |
| Robust to specular/transparent surfaces | **Stereo Anywhere (P021)** | Designed exactly for this case |
| Fastest while still SOTA-tier in-domain | **IGEV-Stereo (P002)** | 12.6M params, 0.18s reported runtime, KITTI-15 D1 1.59 |
| Edge / Jetson deployment | **none of the foundation-VFM models indexed** — fall back to CGI-Stereo / StereoVoxelNet for now | (FM × edge cell empty; see §3.3) |

## §10 Open challenges {#10}

1. **Foundation-VFM × edge deployment** — the indexed FM family
   (FoundationStereo, DEFOM, Stereo Anything, Stereo Anywhere) all run
   on RTX-class GPUs. No Jetson / mobile port indexed.
2. **TensorRT latency missing** (SQ6 confirmed gap). The community
   does not publish TRT engine numbers in abstracts; they live in repo
   READMEs and need grep-extraction (R2-H).
3. **Per-distance accuracy breakdowns** are rare. Most papers report
   only aggregate Mean; the few that disaggregate (P022 PPMStereo for
   temporal, P004 for reflective) are exceptions.
4. **Selective-Stereo's zero-shot regression** (Mean 7.28 vs IGEV's
   5.51, C015) is unexplained — improving in-domain frequency
   handling appears to hurt zero-shot generalization. Open question
   for the field.
5. **Mamba / SSM stereo** has only one indexed paper (P020, ICRA 2026).
   The architectural alternative to Transformer is barely explored.
6. **Synthetic-to-real domain gap** is partially addressed by
   FoundationStereo's 1M synthetic pairs (C011) but is the dominant
   failure mode per Stereo Anywhere's framing (P021).
7. **Benchmark-adoption inertia tracks institutional concentration**
   (C067). The two top-output labs — HUST (3/18 ★★★) and U Bologna
   (3/18) — exhibit opposite habits: HUST's papers stick to canonical
   KITTI/SF/Middlebury/ETH3D; Bologna's introduce emergent datasets
   (Booster, Stereo Anywhere failure modes). The China-cluster
   majority (~11/18 ★★★) inherits the canonical-only habit, which
   means published headline numbers in 2025-2026 still over-index on
   benchmarks that the field's own critical-review papers (P021, P023,
   P025) have shown to mask the dominant failure modes (synthetic-to-
   real, mirrors/transparencies, weather corruption). This is not a
   technical bottleneck but a publication-norm one.

## §11 Key research teams {#11}

Across the 18 ★★★ papers, two institutions hold disproportionate share
of the field's headline output (C067):

- **HUST (Huazhong U of Sci & Tech)** — 3/18 = 17%: P002 IGEV-Stereo
  (CVPR 2023), P003 IGEV++ (TPAMI 2025), P004 Selective-Stereo
  (CVPR 2024). The HUST cluster owns the iterative-geometry-volume
  route end-to-end (geometry-encoding → multi-range → frequency-aware).
- **University of Bologna (Tosi/Mattoccia group)** — 3/18 = 17%: P012
  TemporalStereo (IROS 2023), P017 Survey: Deep Stereo in the Twenties
  (preprint 2024), P021 Stereo Anywhere (CVPR 2025). Bologna owns the
  field-mapping + critical-review angle (taxonomy survey + failure-mode
  paper) and contributes the temporal-stereo lineage.

Combined: **6/18 = 33%** of ★★★ output. The remaining 12 papers spread
across NVIDIA Research (P005), Insta360 (P006), Wuhan U + Bologna multi-
collab (P007), Fudan + Xiaomi + ShanghaiAILab + CUHK (P008), Tongji
(P009), Princeton (P001), Northeastern RIVeR (P016), CityU HK + CUHK SZ
+ Fudan + SYSU (P022), DLUT + Tencent PCG + HKUST GZ (P024), Stuttgart
+ NVIDIA + Mannheim + MPI (P025), Sun Yat-sen (P019), INRIA (P020),
and Beihang + Macquarie + RIKEN + UTokyo (P023).

**Geographic distribution (★★★, n=18, by primary affiliation)**:

- China-affiliated: ~11/18 (61%) — HUST (3), Bologna's Wuhan collab,
  Insta360, Fudan/CUHK clusters, CityU/Sun Yat-sen, DLUT, Tongji
- Europe: ~5/18 (28%) — Bologna (3), Stuttgart (1), INRIA (1)
- US: ~3/18 (17%) — NVIDIA (P005, also on P025), Princeton (P001),
  Northeastern (P016)
- Japan: ~2/18 (11%) — Tokyo Tech (P026), AIST/Tsukuba (P014/P015)

Caveats: many recent papers are multi-institution and double-count;
percentages are share-of-paper not headcount. NVIDIA appears as
collaborator on 2 ★★★ (P005 lead, P025 collab) — the only US-industry
imprint on the canonical set.

**Implications for §3.5 dataset adoption**: HUST's 3 papers all
evaluate on the canonical KITTI/SF/Middlebury/ETH3D set; none adopt
the emergent datasets (RobustSpring, MonoTrap, Mono2Stereo). Bologna
papers are both adopters and producers of emergent datasets (Booster
2023+, Stereo Anywhere's failure-mode evaluations). The canonical-set
inertia thus tracks the geographic split: the China-cluster majority
keeps reporting on canonical benchmarks, while European labs (Bologna,
Stuttgart) drive the emergent-benchmark agenda. This is a structural
finding, not an aesthetic one — it predicts where the next emergent
benchmarks will come from (European groups + a handful of US industry
labs) and where canonical-only model claims will keep accumulating
(the China-cluster lineage).

## §12 Direct Q&A {#12}

**Q: How do edge and foundation stereo matching approaches compare?**

A: They occupy non-overlapping points in the design space. Foundation
models (Mean 2.68 - 3.85, C015) lead in zero-shot accuracy by 2-3×
over the best non-FM method (NMRF Mean 5.15). They cost 18-47M+
trainable params (C013) and 0.25-0.32s/frame on RTX 4090 (C013) — not
edge-feasible without compression. Edge-deployable models (CGI-Stereo,
StereoVoxelNet) trade accuracy for latency but were not benchmarked
on the unified Mean metric in indexed papers.

**Q: Charts for params × accuracy and speed × accuracy?**

A: Generated in `artifacts/`. Chart 1 (params × accuracy) plots 7 of
19 models with grounded numbers. Chart 2 (Torch / proxy) plots the
same 7. Chart 3 (TensorRT) is empty pending repo-grep work.

**Q: Per-data-type analysis?**

A: §9 above. Summary: high-frequency edges → Selective-Stereo;
mirrors/transparencies → Stereo Anywhere; zero-shot generalization →
Stereo Anything; speed-Pareto on RTX → IGEV-Stereo; edge deployment →
no foundation model fits, use CGI-Stereo / StereoVoxelNet.

## §13 Reading list and Round 3 task list {#13}

### Entry tier (3-5 papers, suggested order, ~6h reading)

1. **Survey: Deep Stereo in the Twenties** (P017, ~90 min) — start
   here for the 2020+ taxonomy and term map
2. **RAFT-Stereo** (P001, ~60 min) — 2021 inflection point; recurrent
   field-transform paradigm that everything since 2023 inherits
3. **IGEV-Stereo** (P002, ~60 min) — 2023 hybrid backbone of choice;
   reading this clarifies why "geometry encoding volume" matters
4. **FoundationStereo** (P005, ~90 min) — 2025 foundation wave entry
   point; data-scale shift (1M synthetic pairs) and zero-shot framing

### Deep tier (per architecture route)

- **Recurrent / iterative**: P001 → P002 → P003 (IGEV++) → P010
  (MonSter++)
- **Foundation-VFM**: P005 (data scale) → P006 (frozen DepthAnything
  prior) → P007 (zero-shot champion) → P008 (VFM transfer)
- **Frequency / attention**: P004 Selective-Stereo (frequency-aware
  iteration); P026 Global Occlusion-Aware Transformer
- **SSM / Mamba**: P020 DenVisCoM (sole indexed paper; thin route)
- **Edge / real-time**: P011 CGI-Stereo → P012 TemporalStereo → P013
  Stereo Matching in Time → P016 StereoVoxelNet

### Critical tier (limitations, negative results, failure-mode
papers)

- **P021 Stereo Anywhere** (CVPR 2025) — failure-mode-targeted; only
  paper that explicitly sets out to break foundation-stereo
- **P023 Robust Syn-to-Real Stereo** (CVPR 2024) — synthetic-to-real
  empirical analysis; shows where data-scale alone fails
- **P024 Mono2Stereo** (CVPR 2025) — empirical study of stereo
  conversion; benchmark + critical analysis
- **P025 RobustSpring** (ICLR 2026) — first-class corruption
  benchmark for stereo + scene flow + optical flow; introduces R1px
  metric
- **P022 PPMStereo** (NeurIPS 2025) — dynamic stereo with explicit
  per-distance / temporal-consistency reporting

### Overview tier (other surveys, for cross-checking)

- **P017 Tosi et al., 2024** — only deep-stereo survey within the
  2020+ scope; pair with this survey for triangulation

### Round 3 task list (deferred)

- R3-A (chart-data completion): open paper PDFs for all 18 ★★★
  papers, extract param counts where missing — partially landed in
  iter 1-7 (run 1)
- R3-B (TensorRT data, the SQ6 closure): grep GitHub READMEs of P001
  RAFT-Stereo, P002 IGEV-Stereo, P011 CGI-Stereo, P016 StereoVoxelNet
  for TensorRT / Jetson / FP16 engines — partially landed (iter 1
  C024-C027 + iter 5 C035-C037); the structural gap (TRT numbers
  not in publication norm) documented as Open Challenge #2
- R3-C: extract per-distance breakdowns from P005 / P007 / P022
  appendices when available; pull RobustSpring (P025) corruption-class
  results — landed in iter 6 (PPMStereo, C038-C039) + iter 7
  (RobustSpring R1px, C040-C042)
- ~~R3-D~~ ✅ **closed** (run 2 iter 1-2): institutions backfilled
  for all 18 ★★★ papers (C049-C066); §11 Key Research Teams
  populated with HUST/Bologna concentration narrative + geographic
  split + dataset-adoption implications (C067)

## §14 Reproducibility tier (v1.1 added) {#14}

This section grades each ★★★ paper's evidence provenance per the
5-question rubric in `references/reproducibility-assessment.md`:
release / recipe / issues / quality / 3p reproduction. v1.1 covers 6
flagship papers; the remaining 12 are marked `pending` in
`paper_index.md` and will land in v1.2.

| Paper | Release | Recipe | Issues | Code Quality | 3p Reproduced | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P001 RAFT-Stereo | OSS | complete | 59 open, mixed | strong (Best Student Paper 3DV 2021) | confirmed (OpenStereo Model Zoo matches) | **R1** (C043) |
| P002 IGEV-Stereo | OSS | complete | 36 open, mixed (CN-language community) | strong | confirmed (OpenStereo: 0.46 vs paper 0.47 SF EPE) | **R1** (C044) |
| P004 Selective-Stereo | OSS | complete | 3 open, clean | strong | unverified | **R2** (C045) |
| P005 FoundationStereo | OSS | partial (docker-only TRT) | 75 open, mixed (deployment-pain pattern) | strong (NVIDIA Research) | unverified | **R2-R3** (C046) |
| P006 DEFOM-Stereo | OSS | complete (5 train scripts) | unverified | strong (modular, MIT, Insta360) | unverified | **R1** pending 3p (C047) |
| P021 Stereo Anywhere | OSS | partial (authors: "in development") | 0 open, clean | adequate | unverified | **R2-R3** (C048) |

**Key reproducibility findings**:

1. **All 6 flagships are open-source MIT/permissive** — no closed-code
   work in the foundation-VFM family.
2. **FoundationStereo's 75 open issues skew toward deployment**
   (Jetson, FP16 quantization, monochrome inference, point-cloud
   denoising). The deployment claims (`6× speedup`, C024) need
   third-party validation given this issue pattern.
3. **Stereo Anywhere is author-acknowledged "in-development"** —
   numbers cited from this paper get an explicit caveat in §5.7.
4. **Tier-R1 papers** (RAFT-Stereo, IGEV-Stereo, DEFOM-Stereo)
   provide complete training recipes. Tier-R2 (Selective-Stereo) is
   gold-standard except for missing third-party reproduction.
   Tier-R3 candidates (FoundationStereo, Stereo Anywhere) carry
   recipe / development-stage caveats.
5. **OpenStereo cross-validation** (C033) provides third-party
   reproduction for IGEV (0.46 vs 0.47), confirming P002 numbers.
   No equivalent independent reproduction exists for the foundation
   models yet.

For citation in survey prose: every accuracy / latency claim in §4 /
§6 / §8 from a Tier R3 paper now carries a "(R3 — partial recipe)"
inline. Tier R1/R2 papers cite as before. The chart pipeline does
not yet visualize tier; future v1.2 may add tier-based marker
borders.

## §10.1 Open challenges (v1.1 supplement) {#10-1}

Round 3 surfaced two new open challenges beyond v1's six:

7. **Deployment-claim reproducibility crisis**: claim C024
   (FoundationStereo "6× speedup with TRT FP16") and C034 (OpenStereo
   ships TRT pipeline with zero benchmarks) are now a 2-source pattern:
   the community publishes deployment pipelines but **not benchmarks**.
   Combined with the failure of arXiv `abs:TensorRT` queries to find
   any paper-side numbers, this is structural — not a survey gap.
8. **Foundation-VFM × adversarial corruption robustness untested**:
   RobustSpring (P025) evaluated only RAFT-Stereo / ACVNet / LEAStereo
   / GANet (C040). No foundation-VFM model has been corruption-graded.
   This is a Round 4 follow-up gap.

## §6.1 Cross-method speed-track (v1.1 added) {#6-1}

Two distinct evaluation regimes have surfaced:

| Regime | Y axis | Best example |
|---|---|---|
| **Zero-shot Mean** (chart 1 / 2) | KITTI / Middlebury / ETH3D / KITTI Mean (lower better) | StereoAnything 2.68 (C015) |
| **Speed-track** (KITTI-finetuned, <50ms class) | KITTI 2015 D1-all (lower better) | HITNet 20ms / 1.98 D1-all (C035) |
| **Temporal consistency** | TEPE (Sintel, Dynamic Replica) | PPMStereo_VDA 0.052 TEPE (C038) |
| **Corruption robustness** | R1px (RobustSpring) | RAFT-Stereo (s) avg 33.40 (C040) |

These four regimes capture different deployment realities and **do
not collapse to one Y axis**. The chart pipeline currently visualizes
only the first regime; the others are textual in this v1.1.
